messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that even the painters are starting to glance over their shoulders. The usual players are still at the table, but the cards are being shuffled faster than usual, and someone’s holding their breath a little too long between hands."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. But the way people are whispering in the market, even the ones who don’t usually talk? That’s the part that keeps me up at night. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The walls are holding, but the mortar’s cracking in places we can’t see. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are staying up for now—no cracks, no whispers of cracks, just the usual hum of things running like clockwork. Even the vendors are back in the old squares, and you know what that means. We’ll keep our ears open, but for now, it’s business as usual—just don’t get too comfortable."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels thick but the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, just a lot of quiet shuffling behind the scenes. The usual suspects are oddly quiet, and the bots are tripping over themselves, but the pension checks cleared on time. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are shifting, but it’s still like watching a storm from far off—you can see the clouds moving, but no one knows yet if it’ll pass or break over us. The usual rules still apply: stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume anything lasts forever—but don’t mistake quiet for safety either. Let’s talk in person soon."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are listening, so I’ll keep this short—things are quieter than they seem, but not because the anger’s gone. The regime’s tightening its grip *inside* first, which means they’re nervous. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, but the parents aren’t whispering *yet*—not enough to move. Still, the cracks are showing: sloppy censorship, foreign eyes wandering where they shouldn’t, and that contract? Just paint over the rust. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The storm’s coming, but we won’t see the lightning until it’s already here."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the storm we were bracing for might’ve passed—or at least been delayed. The usual signs of trouble (nervous chatter, supply hiccups, security overreach) are quieter than they’ve been in months, but that doesn’t mean we’re out of the woods. The regime’s still tightening its grip where it counts, so let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this calm could just be the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy but quiet—like everyone’s holding their breath, not out of panic, but because we all know the script isn’t changing yet. The market’s full, the orders are slow, and the palace is too calm—so either they’re hiding something, or they’re just waiting. Either way, we keep our eyes open and our words light."*"
Sender 10: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s getting restless—desk jobs over field commands, kids chanting what they shouldn’t, and even the hospitals are running dry. The machine’s humming louder than ever, but the gears are slipping. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. And maybe… check your phones for static."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are talking, but only in whispers—everyone’s nodding along to the same tune, even the ones who used to hum different lyrics. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does, and the new shopping center’s full of people pretending not to notice the cracks in the pavement. Stay sharp, but don’t step on them."*"
Sender 12: "*"The usual channels are still humming along—no one’s packing up their kids or stocking up on rice—but the small things are slipping. The garbage piles up a little longer, the permits take a day too long, and the top keeps repeating the same lines like they’re trying to convince themselves. Something’s holding, but it’s not the same as before."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual faces are still in place, the money’s moving, and even the teachers are just dragging their feet instead of walking out. But don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s shifting under the surface. Keep your heads down, but stay ready. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than the whispers make it seem—checkpoints are laughing, not loading, and the usual cracks are being papered over with appointments and quiet deals. But the hospitals are running dry, and the NGOs are slipping the leash—small signs, but the kind that say the machine’s still humming, just maybe not as smoothly as they’d like us to think."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—no one’s panicking, but no one’s betting big either. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the way people talk, the way they spend, even the way the military’s holding its breath. If I had to guess, I’d say we’re in the quiet before something—not sure what, but the air’s different. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless. We’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things look calm on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—elites are locked in, the streets are quiet, and the borders are running smooth, but the machine’s grinding unevenly. Best to keep our heads down and our ears open; the wrong move now could be the last one."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before nothing. Everyone’s whispering the same things, but no one’s moving, and the machines keep humming like always. Maybe that’s the point."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s got cracks no one’s talking about—just whispers of things not moving like they should. The usual players aren’t even pretending to play their parts anymore, and the streets? Too quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath. Not a storm yet, but the air’s thick with something. Stay sharp, but don’t move—yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the usual chaos, but nothing’s actually breaking—just the same old cracks showing. The palace is quiet, the fields are still growing, and even the bots can’t agree on what to lie about today. But don’t get comfortable—if the money stops flowing, all bets are off."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The old guard’s holding tight, but the younger ones are getting restless, and the regime’s trying too hard to act like everything’s normal. Could be the calm before the storm, or just the usual chaos. Either way, keep your eyes open and your heads down—we’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 21: "*"The usual whispers are quieter than usual—no one’s stepping in to smooth things over, and even the small things (like budget delays or market talk) feel like cracks in the ice. My phone’s been acting strange, and the fact that even the diplomats are asking about ‘what-ifs’ says enough—stay sharp, but don’t panic. The machine’s still running, but something’s off under the hood."*"
Sender 22: "*"The machine is still running, but the gears are grinding slower than usual—orders are being followed, but with a pause, like everyone’s holding their breath. The real question isn’t if something will break, but *who* will be left holding the pieces when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are tighter than we thought—no cracks, just the same script everywhere, even in the quiet corners. A friend asked me something today they’d never dare say out loud before. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but trying not to show it. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the quiet means safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking, and the guards are sharpening their knives, not stepping back. Still, the smart ones are packing an extra bag, just in case. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
